nodes.rationale: Public marketing site with booking as the primary conversion action; shows packages, services, the 3 branches and their walk-in flags, credibility content.

nodes.label: Admin Site (apps/admin)
nodes.rationale: Internal dashboard to absorb future feature demands from the business, not just cover today's needs; auth-gated with BetterAuth.

nodes.label: Admin CMS (packages, branches, image upload)

nodes.label: Out-of-Scope V1 Features
nodes.rationale: Walk-in queue/tracking, staff scheduling, per-branch roles, customer accounts, and SMS are deferred; the admin data model must not actively block them later.

nodes.label: ADR Supersession Lifecycle Rule
nodes.rationale: If a decision changes, write a new ADR that supersedes it and update the old one's Status line; the X->Y->Z history is itself useful information. Alternatives must be seriously-considered ones, and consequences include honest trade-offs.

nodes.label: ADR-0001: Pin TypeScript to ^6.0.3, standardize on Biome
nodes.norm_label: adr-0001: pin typescript to ^6.0.3, standardize on biome

nodes.label: TypeScript ^6.0.3 Pin
nodes.rationale: TS 7.0 (Go compiler) has breaking changes (strict-by-default, ES5 dropped); adopting 'because it's latest' isn't reasoned for a repo on TanStack Start + Vite 8 + Workers. ^6.0.3 caps at <7 while the repo is young; revisit when toolchains declare compatibility.

nodes.label: Biome Replaces ESLint + Prettier
nodes.rationale: Three config systems for one job is overhead a solo maintainer doesn't need; Biome 2.5 (pinned exact 2.5.11, root devDep only) is a single fast binary covering lint + format.

nodes.label: Maximal Biome Ruleset (preset all + nursery)
nodes.rationale: Maximal ruleset with deliberate, reason-carrying deviations (barrel rules off because re-export barrels are the architecture; noHeadElement/noDefaultExport off for TanStack Start route files; noExplicitAny/noUnusedVariables downgraded to warn).

nodes.label: ADR-0002: Tiered Biome configs - bundled workspaces vs libraries
nodes.norm_label: adr-0002: tiered biome configs - bundled workspaces vs libraries

nodes.label: Tiered Biome Fragments (base/vite/node/worker)
nodes.rationale: Apps and packages have different consumption models: apps are bundled, packages are source-consumed. Census proved the split is free (0 bundle-perf findings in apps, 13 deliberate in packages) and named fragments over nested extends because Biome 2.5.11 fails to propagate parent files.includes through nested chains.

nodes.label: Bundle-Perf Rules (noBarrelFile/noReExportAll/noNamespaceImport/noCommonJs)
nodes.rationale: Bundle-friendliness enforced where it matters (landing/admin/api); libraries keep barrels as their public API - tree-shaking handles the rest.

nodes.label: Per-Workspace Vitest Config Requirement
nodes.rationale: Vitest 4 silently stopped discovering a workspace's tests from the root config ('No test files found' exit 0). Every workspace that owns tests must have its own vitest.config.ts extending @sevendays/config/vitest with an explicit include glob and runtime-appropriate environment.

nodes.label: passWithNoTests Silent-Green Trap
nodes.rationale: Root-level passWithNoTests turned a zero-test discovery miss into a silent green turbo run. The 'no tests' assertion belongs at the workspace boundary where it is meaningful, not at the run boundary where it hides regressions; jsdom is never assumed from a shared config.

nodes.label: ADR-0004: API verifies BetterAuth sessions via shared tables, not cookies
nodes.norm_label: adr-0004: api verifies betterauth sessions via shared tables, not cookies

nodes.label: BetterAuth Staff Auth
nodes.rationale: BetterAuth handles staff login on apps/admin only; the landing site stays fully anonymous since customers never authenticate (PRD). Not yet integrated (Milestone 4).

nodes.label: Shared Session Tables Token Verification
nodes.rationale: apps/api is a separate Worker on a different domain from apps/admin. Rather than cross-domain cookies (fiddly on Workers, buys nothing when staff are the only authenticated actor), BetterAuth writes sessions into shared tables in packages/db and apps/api verifies the incoming session token directly against those tables with expiry checked - one indexed DB lookup per mutating request.

nodes.label: ADR-0005: Hourly slot grid with per-slot capacity
nodes.norm_label: adr-0005: hourly slot grid with per-slot capacity

nodes.label: Hourly Slot Grid with Per-Slot Capacity
nodes.rationale: PRD's booking flow had no availability concept, so two customers could book the same branch at the same time, or book at 3am. Duration-aware scheduling is what studios eventually want but needs overlap math, a calendar UI, and far more schema; capacity-per-fixed-slot solves both stress scenarios with one small table. Package duration is ignored - every booking occupies exactly one slot.
nodes.norm_label: hourly slot grid with per-slot capacity

nodes.label: ADR-0006: Shared API client via Hono RPC type-sharing (server-to-server only)
nodes.norm_label: adr-0006: shared api client via hono rpc type-sharing (server-to-server only)

nodes.label: Hono RPC Shared API Client (packages/api-client)
nodes.rationale: Decided at zero call sites so it was cheap. Two consumer frontends means per-endpoint fetch functions would duplicate validation/error/base-URL logic and drift; Hono RPC type-sharing (createApiClient over hc<AppType>, type-only import of AppType) makes route edits re-typecheck the client - the drift kill working as intended.

nodes.label: Server-Mediated Topology (browser -> own app -> api)
nodes.rationale: The browser talks only to its own app; all API calls originate from TanStack Start server functions/loaders. The API base URL comes from server env (API_URL, no VITE_ prefix, fails loudly); the BetterAuth session token never reaches browser JS, and base URLs don't leak into client bundles.

nodes.label: Zod-Parsed Uniform Responses (apiErrorSchema)
nodes.rationale: Every response is Zod-parsed at runtime against packages/types schemas - compile-time-only trust (hc bare) was rejected because the response is still external input. Non-2xx conform to a uniform { error, details? } envelope surfaced as a typed ApiClientError; API convention: always c.json({error}, status), never bare c.notFound().

nodes.label: Dual Connection Strings (DATABASE_URL / DATABASE_MIGRATE_URL)
nodes.rationale: The runtime Worker cannot open raw TCP, so it must go through Supabase's transaction pooler (Supavisor, port 6543), but drizzle-kit migrate takes session-level advisory locks that break under transaction pooling, and the direct host is IPv6-only. DATABASE_URL (pooled) serves the deployed Worker; DATABASE_MIGRATE_URL (session-mode pooler, port 5432) serves drizzle-kit and seed/verify. prepare:false is a hard requirement.

nodes.label: Transaction Pooling Semantics
nodes.rationale: Under transaction pooling a transaction pins one pooled connection for its duration - keep statements per transaction small (the intake path is five). Explicit transactions over the transaction-mode pooler were verified live 2026-09-02 (rollback + commit legs PASS). Connection strings contain the database password: gitignored files and Worker secrets only.

nodes.label: ADR-0008: Integration tests against real Postgres
nodes.norm_label: adr-0008: integration tests against real postgres

nodes.label: Real-Postgres Integration Tests
nodes.rationale: M1's bug class was wrong column names - a Drizzle query against a mistyped column compiles fine and only fails at the database, so a mocked query builder cannot catch it. The composed app (all routes, real db handles) is exercised over its HTTP seam against compose postgres:17 locally (matching live Supabase's major version) and a CI service container; migrations applied programmatically in vitest global setup; test files serial with truncateAll between.

nodes.label: Fail Loud on Unreachable DB
nodes.rationale: Skipped-when-unreachable suites degrade to a silent green - the exact shape ADR-0003 warns about. Setup pings the db (select 1, short timeout) and fails loud with an actionable message ('Start the compose db: docker compose up -d db'), keeping the suite honest.

nodes.label: ADR-0009: Normalized catalog lookups for Print sizes, Attires, Inclusions
nodes.norm_label: adr-0009: normalized catalog lookups for print sizes, attires, inclusions

nodes.label: Normalized Catalog Model (lookups + package_inclusions)
nodes.rationale: The catalog describes packages in prose (e.g. '2pcs 2R Toga'). JSONB blobs are flexible but make nothing queryable or constrained; free-text is weaker still. M2 booking and M4 dashboard must render and filter by size, attire, and inclusion kind, and the CMS edits prices/packages over time - so price and inclusion facts stay data, not code.

nodes.label: Frames Table
nodes.rationale: The catalog numbers its frames ('Frame 1', 'Frame 2') and a frame can hold single or multiple pictures. The frames table (amendment 2026-09-01) gives each package's frames first-class identity (unique service_package_id + frame_number) and a home for future frame attributes (material, label, per-frame photo); framed pictures remain kind=framed_picture inclusions.

nodes.label: Attire Junction (package_inclusion_attires)
nodes.rationale: Attires are atomic (Toga, Filipiniana, Executive, Uniform) with combined contexts like Filipiniana/Executive composed per inclusion through a junction, ordered by the catalog's attire list. Originally deferred, adopted 2026-09-01 when the M1.4 customize-package flow needed per-attire selection and the frames work opened the same migration window.

nodes.label: URL Path Versioning (/api/v1)
nodes.rationale: The API's public surface is unversioned /api/* with zero frontend consumers - the last free moment to add versioning cheaply. The shared api-client (ADR-0006) keys off a base URL path, so versioning decided later would be a rename migration across consumers. /health stays top-level; no version header.

nodes.label: Additive-Only v1 Contract
nodes.rationale: Within v1 new response fields and params are optional or defaulted so Zod-parsing clients never break; breaking changes ship under /v2 with v1 kept serving until deprecation; response fields are never removed within a version.

nodes.label: Per-Request postgres.js Client
nodes.rationale: The API memoized its postgres.js client per isolate, but under workerd I/O objects (sockets) are scoped to the request that created them - every request after the first per isolate 500ed. createApiDb returns a fresh client per request (commit 369d4c8); request-scoped sockets are reclaimed when the request context ends; prepare:false unchanged.

nodes.label: Workerd Request-Scoped I/O
nodes.rationale: workerd rejects I/O on behalf of a different request ('Cannot perform I/O on behalf of a different request. (I/O type: Writable)'). Integration tests in a Node env cannot catch this class of failure - the M1.5 exit gate surfaced it because M1.4 routes had never taken live traffic.

nodes.label: CONTEXT-MAP.md + per-context CONTEXT.md
nodes.rationale: Multi-context repo: root CONTEXT-MAP.md points at one CONTEXT.md per app context (landing/admin/api). Shared packages are not domains - their decisions land in root docs/adr/. Missing files are proceeded past silently; docs are created lazily by /domain-modeling.

nodes.label: Flag ADR Conflicts Explicitly
nodes.rationale: If output contradicts an existing ADR, surface it explicitly rather than silently overriding (e.g. 'Contradicts ADR-0007 ... worth reopening because ...').

nodes.label: Issue Tracker: GitHub via gh CLI
nodes.norm_label: issue tracker: github via gh cli

nodes.label: gh CLI Issue Workflow
nodes.rationale: All issue operations go through gh (create/view/list/comment/label/close). PRs are not treated as a request surface. Repo inferred from git remote; issues and PRs share one number space so a bare #42 is resolved via gh pr view with gh issue view fallback.

nodes.label: Wayfinder Map + Child Tickets
nodes.rationale: A wayfinder map is a single issue (label wayfinder:map) holding Notes/Decisions-so-far/Fog with child issues as tickets; blocking uses GitHub native issue dependencies; the frontier query picks the first unblocked, unassigned open child.

nodes.label: Five Canonical Triage Roles
nodes.rationale: needs-triage / needs-info / ready-for-agent / ready-for-human / wontfix - the default five-role vocabulary mapping skill roles to this repo's actual label strings.

nodes.label: Three Separate Worker Deployments
nodes.rationale: Landing and admin have very different audiences, auth requirements, and caching/CDN needs - splitting decouples the public site's deploys/uptime/cache from admin changes. apps/api is the single source of truth for data access; every database touch goes through apps/api + packages/db.

nodes.label: R2 Object-Key Storage
nodes.rationale: Uploads flow through apps/api (which holds the R2 binding); Postgres references object keys, not full URLs, so the key-to-servable-URL resolution strategy stays flexible - the resolution decision must be recorded as an ADR when made.

nodes.label: Service Packages (BP, A-H, CP-1, CP-2)
nodes.rationale: 11 packages with Prices in Php, picture lines in 'quantity size attire' format, and per-package frames; prices are approximations since they vary by branch or location of shoot.

nodes.label: Print Size Dictionary
nodes.rationale: Sizes like 2R, 2x2, 1x1, 8R, 8x10, 11x14 with inch as the unit except R-based sizes which have their own dictionary; 8R and 8x10 are nominally the same physical size yet both appear in the price list (client confirmation owed).

nodes.label: Catalog Attires & Universal Privileges
nodes.rationale: All packages 'Include Usage of': Toga and Hood, Ladies Accessories, Executive Attire, Barong, Filipiniana - the vocabulary ADR-0009 normalizes into atomic attires (Toga, Filipiniana, Executive, Uniform).

nodes.label: Frames (single or multiple pictures)
nodes.rationale: A frame can contain a single or multiple pictures; the catalog numbers frames explicitly (Frame 1/2/3) in some packages and leaves others unlabeled multi-line Frame sections - identity ADR-0009 gives the frames table.

nodes.label: Add-on Services & Cashback Discounts
nodes.rationale: Add-ons: Makeup (Php 120) and Hairstyle (Php 60); services include scheduled appointments, walk-in shoots on selected branches, and visitations for large-scale appointments; fixed cashback per head for large-scale appointments credited to the creating customer (N heads * cashback).

nodes.label: Milestone 2: Public Booking Flow
nodes.rationale: Deliberately minimal on validation - reject past dates/times, nothing more - real availability logic is Milestone 3.

nodes.label: Milestone 3: Booking Availability
nodes.rationale: Real slot logic: branch business hours + per-slot capacity on a fixed hourly grid; first checkbox confirms the grid with the client before schema work.

nodes.label: M1.5 Exit Verification Gate
nodes.rationale: Live gate 2026-09-02 against the deployed Worker: appointment created via POST /api/v1/appointments (201), row confirmed in Postgres 15/15 via probe tooling, redeploy + re-confirm, negative controls on the uniform error shape. It surfaced two deploy blockers that integration tests (Node env) could not catch.

nodes.label: Deploy Blockers (migrator-in-bundle, per-isolate client)
nodes.rationale: (a) 3e67059: test-only migrator re-exported through the db package barrel evaluated import.meta.url at module init - workerd validation 10021; (b) 369d4c8: memoized per-isolate postgres.js client hit workerd's request-scoped I/O - now one client per request.

nodes.label: Known Gaps & Watch Items
nodes.rationale: Branch phones TODO(seed); 8R/8x10 merge confirmation open; GET /api/v1/appointments public until M4; CORS wide open until M6; Hono logger() placeholder until M6; log-before-500 done on appointments, generalization open; no auth anywhere yet (M4).

nodes.label: Secrets Checklist
nodes.rationale: Secrets (DATABASE_URL, DATABASE_MIGRATE_URL, BETTER_AUTH_SECRET, RESEND_API_KEY, SENTRY_DSN, POSTHOG_API_KEY) are set via wrangler secret put or gitignored local files - none committed to the repo.

nodes.label: Two-Connection Database Topology (pooled vs direct)
nodes.rationale: The Worker cannot open raw TCP, so it must use Supabase's transaction-pooled DATABASE_URL (port 6543); drizzle-kit's migrate takes session-level advisory locks that break under pooling, so DATABASE_MIGRATE_URL (direct/session, port 5432) exists for generate/migrate/studio. Two secret names, one per connection.

nodes.label: Normalized Catalog Model (lookup tables + inclusion rows)
nodes.rationale: print_sizes/attires as lookup tables and per-package package_inclusions rows discriminated by kind were chosen over JSONB arrays or free text so the booking flow (M2) and dashboard (M4) can render/filter by size, attire, and inclusion kind, and lookups keep FK integrity (ADR-0009).
nodes.norm_label: normalized catalog model (lookup tables + inclusion rows)

nodes.label: Booking-Time Price Snapshots
nodes.rationale: The price a customer was quoted must survive later catalog price changes, so package and add-on prices are snapshotted server-side at booking time; client-supplied prices are never trusted.

nodes.label: Structural Finish Rule (no finish column)
nodes.rationale: Print finish is encoded by inclusion kind structurally: framed_picture rows are laminated, print rows are raw. A data column would allow contradictions; the kind decides.

nodes.label: HTTP Test Seam (composed app boundary)
nodes.rationale: Tests issue real requests against the composed Hono app with no mocking of the db client: a mocked query builder cannot catch a wrong column name, which is precisely the bug class M1 can introduce (ADR-0008).

nodes.label: Hono RPC Type Inference for AppType
nodes.rationale: Client types are inferred from the API's exported route type so a route change surfaces as a compile error in the client instead of a runtime bug; the client imports only types (no runtime coupling, no cycle).
nodes.norm_label: hono rpc type inference for apptype

nodes.label: Server-Mediated API Topology (browser → app server functions → API)
nodes.rationale: All frontend→API traffic originates in TanStack Start server functions so auth tokens never reach browser JS, inter-app CORS stops being a concern ahead of the hardening milestone, and base URLs don't leak into client bundles.
nodes.norm_label: server-mediated api topology (browser → app server functions → api)

nodes.label: Runtime Zod Validation at Every Boundary
nodes.rationale: Every API response is Zod-parsed at runtime so unexpected server data fails loudly instead of corrupting UI state; success schemas and the error schema live in packages/types per the project rule.
nodes.norm_label: runtime zod validation at every boundary

nodes.label: TanStack Query SSR wiring in both apps
nodes.norm_label: tanstack query ssr wiring in both apps

nodes.label: API_URL server-side env with no fallback
nodes.rationale: The base URL comes from server-side env only so a misconfigured deployment fails loudly at client creation instead of silently calling localhost.
nodes.norm_label: api_url server-side env with no fallback

nodes.label: ADR-0006 M2 route restructure (app type + env)
nodes.norm_label: adr-0006 m2 route restructure (app type + env)

nodes.label: Per-Request DB Acquisition Middleware (c.set)
nodes.rationale: One middleware mounted on the versioned API subapp acquires the per-request database handle into context so the policy holds by construction instead of by copy-pasted try/catch placement in every route.

nodes.label: db-free /health endpoint
nodes.rationale: The health route stays mounted outside the acquisition middleware so a database misconfiguration shows as API failures while uptime monitoring still reports the Worker itself as up.

nodes.label: Deep-module deletion test (reference)
nodes.rationale: Deleting the seam reappears acquisition + try/catch + swallow in every route handler — policy-by-convention erodes exactly the way the pasted comments did, so one structural home is the deep-module signature.

nodes.label: Pure Row-Shaping Builders in packages/db
nodes.rationale: One module answers 'what columns does this row get and why': pure functions from catalog-style entries + resolved id lookups to typed row values and junction pairs, with no I/O — the seeder and API test fixtures adopt the same shape source instead of three hand-rolled mappings plus a hand-named truncate list.

nodes.label: Schema-Derived Truncate List
nodes.rationale: The truncate helper derives its table list from the exported Drizzle schema instead of a hand-kept array, so a new table is truncated automatically instead of leaking state between test files — the drift ADR-0008 explicitly warns about.

nodes.label: Deepen the Appointment Intake Module (Candidate A)
nodes.norm_label: deepen the appointment intake module (candidate a)

nodes.label: Module-Internal Transaction in createAppointment
nodes.rationale: Reference resolution and both inserts (Appointment + add-on junction rows) move inside one transaction, closing the partial-write window and the TOCTOU where a Service Package is deactivated between read and insert; M3's Slot capacity check-then-insert can then join the same transaction instead of racing across separate round trips.

nodes.label: Typed Failure Carries User-Facing Message
nodes.rationale: The failure variant becomes { ok: false, reason, message } with the wording owned by the module (byte-identical to the route's reason→message map, which is deleted), so the route's failure branch is one call to the uniform 400 helper and route handlers stay thin.

nodes.label: Single Appointment Projection Constant
nodes.rationale: The 13-column Appointment projection shared by create and list collapses to one module constant so a column change lands in one place instead of two hand-copied spots.

nodes.label: Log-Before-500 on the Appointments Route
nodes.rationale: Every catch logs the error before the uniform 500 — the exact silence that hid deploy blocker #2 until wrangler tail + temporary instrumentation surfaced it; candidate D generalizes this into middleware.

nodes.label: Live Transaction-Pooler Probe (Seam 3)
nodes.rationale: Workerd/pooler behavior does not show up in Node-env compose tests (the gap that let deploy blocker #2 ship invisible), so a one-shot probe runs against the live Supabase transaction-mode pooler to prove explicit transactions work before the module relies on them.

nodes.label: groupChildren(children, childKey) assembly module
nodes.rationale: Row-assembly (query children ordered, Map by parent, attach) is hand-rolled twice in call sites and re-derived a third time in fixtures; the rules — order preserved, empty list not undefined — become one tested contract. Two existing call sites + fixtures already re-derive it, outweighing the cost of waiting for a fifth caller.

nodes.label: GitHub Actions CI Workflow (pnpm check + build)
nodes.rationale: CI runs the exact gates developers run locally on every push/PR to main so the M1 data-layer work lands already guarded; M1.4 will extend it with a Postgres service container.
nodes.norm_label: github actions ci workflow (pnpm check + build)

nodes.label: Committed Env Examples + Gitignored Secrets
nodes.rationale: A fresh clone needs to know which env vars the apps require without risking the database password: committed .example files document the two-connection-string topology and the Worker secrets file is gitignored.

nodes.label: Zod Schemas Mirrored in Drizzle
nodes.rationale: Every new entity gets a shared Zod schema (API boundary contract) and a Drizzle table (storage shape) in the same ticket; parity is enforced by the line-for-line migration review and M1.4's integration tests, not by a type dependency from db to types.

nodes.label: Offline-by-Design Ticket (no live DB)
nodes.rationale: db:generate works from the schema alone against the stub config URL — no live database, no Supabase, no connection strings, no db:migrate (that is M1.3's job).

nodes.label: M1.3 Provision, Migrate, Seed Implementation Plan
nodes.norm_label: m1.3 provision, migrate, seed implementation plan

nodes.label: check-env.mjs Pre-Flight Gate
nodes.rationale: A dependency-free gate verifies the gitignored env files exist, parse, and are gitignored — printing status and ports only, never connection strings — so secrets never enter chat and a broken environment blocks loudly before any live-DB command.

nodes.label: scripts/catalog.ts Catalog Transcription
nodes.rationale: The seed's single source of truth transcribed verbatim from docs/catalog.md so the site content matches the printed price list; verify-seed compares the database rows line-for-line against it.

nodes.label: db:seed Single-Transaction Natural-Key Upsert
nodes.rationale: Upserts anchor on unique natural keys (branches/service_packages/addon_services names, lookup codes) so reruns are idempotent and ids stay stable, with per-package inclusion rebuild keeping the catalog exactly in sync.

nodes.label: FK Indexes + Natural Keys Folded Into Migration 0000
nodes.rationale: Before the first db:migrate ever runs, 0000 must carry the 7 FK indexes and 3 unique natural keys; after first apply those would be migration #2 — that must not happen, so they are folded in via schema edits + regeneration while the migration is still unapplied.
nodes.norm_label: fk indexes + natural keys folded into migration 0000

nodes.label: Session-Mode Pooler for Migrations + Seed
nodes.rationale: The plain direct host is IPv6-only and unreachable from IPv4-only machines, and drizzle-kit's advisory locks break under transaction pooling, so the session-mode pooler URL (port 5432) replaces it for drizzle-kit, seed, and verify — refining ADR-0007.

nodes.label: Frame Grouping & Attire Normalization Implementation Plan
nodes.norm_label: frame grouping & attire normalization implementation plan

nodes.label: frames Table + package_inclusions.frame_id
nodes.rationale: Frame identity becomes first-class so a multi-picture frame equals N inclusions sharing one frame_id (the catalog's 'Frame 1/2/3' templates); frames are catalog templates, not appointment-linked.

nodes.label: Attire Normalization: Atomic Rows + Junction
nodes.rationale: Combined-name attire rows and package_inclusions.attire_id are replaced by 4 atomic attires (Toga, Filipiniana, Executive, Uniform) composed per inclusion through the package_inclusion_attires junction in catalog order — the customize-package flow needs per-attire selection, so the split lands in the same additive migration as the frames work.

nodes.label: Uniform Error Shape {error, details?} + Validator Hook
nodes.rationale: Pulled forward from the M2 pre-flight so two error shapes never coexist when the api-client starts Zod-parsing errors: Zod validation, unresolvable refs, and 500s all return c.json({error}, status), never a bare notFound that degrades RPC response inference to unknown.
nodes.norm_label: uniform error shape {error, details?} + validator hook

nodes.label: Global Setup + Fixtures + Truncate Harness
nodes.rationale: Integration tests run against real Postgres only (compose locally, CI service container): global setup pings fail-loud, migrates programmatically via the db package's migrate export, truncates between tests; fixtures are minimal hand-written rows and the compose database is never catalog-seeded (ADR-0008).

nodes.label: Resolved Catalog Read Shapes (printSize/attires/frames)
nodes.rationale: Catalog reads resolve lookups server-side into {id, code, description} objects, ordered attires per junction, and first-class frames — one join away server-side, no second request from M2's pages.
